keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the Kingdom of Hungary and Kingdom of Bohemia shapes draw Slovakia). Charles's coronation in 1301 is the page's basis for Matthew's hold on Trenčín and Nitra counties, with Komárno and Senica inherited and Trenčín acquired in 1296. The page gives no area.

correction.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

keyframe_review.note: 'By that time, 14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles were under his and his followers' rule' (the page places this around 1311, before Rozgony); the Kingdom of Hungary dossier reads the 14 counties as the lands now forming Slovakia.

region.text: the royal castles of Trenčín and Nyitra (Nitra) counties, with Komárno and Senica inherited c. 1283

ledger.note: 1301: the Árpád line ends (Andrew III died on 14 January 1301) and Matthew III Csák, who inherited Komárno and Senica c. 1283 and acquired Trenčín around the end of 1296, holds the royal castles of Trenčín and Nitra counties from Charles's coronation of 1301. The year and counties are the page's, the extent my reading.

region.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

ledger.note: c. 1311: his peak. 'By that time, 14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles were under his and his followers' rule.' The page dates the extent only 'before Rozgony'; the region (Slovakia) is the Kingdom of Hungary dossier's reading.

region.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

ledger.note: 25 June 1311: Matthew raids toward Buda (the cardinal excommunicated him on 6 July); royal forces liberate Sáros in 1311. Fighting between the king and Matthew follows: Rozgony on 15 June 1312, invasions in 1314-1315.
1315: Visegrád is 'occupied by Charles's forces'; John of Bohemia invaded his lands in May 1315 and defeated his troops at Holics.

region.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

ledger.note: 1321: 'Matthew Csák's former domain was overtaken by the king's armies in a few months' time' after his death on 18 March 1321; his cousin Stephen Sternberg took over briefly.

ledger.note: 1321: the domain falls to the royal armies within months of Matthew's death.

wars.name: War of Charles I of Hungary against Matthew III Csák

zones.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

wars.outcome: Charles I's army defeated Matthew and his allies at Rozgony on 15 June 1312, invaded his lands in 1314-1315 (John of Bohemia at Holics in May 1315, Visegrád) and overtook the domain in a few months after Matthew's death on 18 March 1321.
wars.note: The page also records the 1317 invasion of the Nyitra diocese and the second excommunication.

certainty.note: The page counts '14 counties' and 'about 50 castles', not a boundary; the lands were a patchwork of castles and followers.

sources.title: Matthew III Csák
sources.note: Offices, castles, 14 counties and about 50 castles c. 1311, Rozgony 15 June 1312, 1314-1317, death 18 March 1321, the aftermath.

notes:
A rebel domain Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-c: 'Domain of Matthew III Csak (Slovak counties) [1301, 1321]'). Slug follows slug.py for 'Domain of Matthew III Csák' (the eu-15-c suggestion matthew-iii-csak is the person). The Kingdom of Hungary dossier names the counterpart as the string 'Matthew III Csak'; it should now name this slug, and its 1305 loss date is not on the page I read (events 1301, 1311). One page only (budget 1-2).

Not settled: (1) the extent in 1301-1310: the page names castles (Trenčín, Nitra counties, Komárno, Senica, Vöröskő, Beckov, Sáros, Jókő, Sirok, Fülek), not counties; the 14 counties are undated ('by that time', about 1311). (2) The page gives 18 March 1321 for the death. (3) 1316-1317 losses (Jókő) are not booked. (4) Type rebel is my choice: he was palatine in 1302-1309 and reappointed in 1308, and fought the king from 1311.
